00477| ## Quick Setup
00478| 
00479| ```bash
00480| # One-liner to initialize and apply (installs chezmoi to ~/.local/bin)
00481| export GITHUB_USERNAME=daviddwlee84
00482| sh -c "$(curl -fsLS get.chezmoi.io)" -- -b "$HOME/.local/bin" init --apply git@github.com:$GITHUB_USERNAME/dotfiles.git
00483| ```
00484| 
00485| This automatically:
00486| 
00487| 1. Bootstraps Homebrew (macOS/Linux), uv, mise, ansible
00488| 2. Deploys all config files
00489| 3. Runs ansible playbooks (git, ripgrep, fd, neovim, etc.)
00490| 4. Runs brew bundle (if `installBrewApps` enabled)
00491| 
00492| ### Optional Components
00493| 
00494| During `chezmoi init`, you'll be prompted for optional installs:
00495| 
00496| | Option | Default | Description |
00497| |--------|---------|-------------|
00498| | `installCodingAgents` | true | Claude Code, OpenCode, Cursor, Copilot, Gemini CLI, etc. |
00499| | `installBitwarden` | false | Bitwarden CLI (`bw`) + Desktop app (desktop profiles) with SSH agent auto-detection |
00500| | `installPythonUvTools` | true | Python CLI tools via uv (mlflow, litellm, sqlit-tui, etc.) |
00501| | `installBrewApps` | false | GUI apps via Homebrew Brewfile (casks, mas) |
00502| | `noRoot` | false | Skip sudo-requiring tasks (for servers without root access) |
00503| 
00504| To change options later: `chezmoi init --force`
00505| 
00506| ## What You Get
00507| 
00508| ### Config Files
00509| 
00510| - `~/.gitconfig` - Git configuration
00511| - `~/.config/nvim/` - Neovim (LazyVim) configuration
00512| - `~/.config/uv/uv.toml` - uv package manager config
00513| - `~/.cargo/config.toml` - Cargo registry mirror config (GFW)
00514| - `~/.npmrc` - npm registry config (official/npmmirror via `useChineseMirror`)
00515| - `~/.config/.bunfig.toml` - Bun global registry config (official/npmmirror via `useChineseMirror`)
00516| - `~/.config/alacritty/` - Alacritty terminal config
00517| - `~/.claude/` - Claude Code settings
00518| - `~/.tmux.conf` - Tmux configuration with TPM plugins
00519| - `~/.local/bin/x` - Cross-platform terminal wrapper for `copy` / `paste` / `open`
00520| - `~/.config/zsh/tools/36_pueue.zsh` - Pueue queue summary helper (`pqsum`)
00521| - `~/.config/zsh/tools/28_tldr.zsh` - `tldrf` helper with `TLDR_LANGUAGES` fallback order
00522| - `~/.config/zsh/tools/95_bitwarden.zsh` - Bitwarden CLI completion + SSH agent socket auto-detection
00523| - `~/.ssh/config` - SSH main config skeleton (create-only: `Include ~/.ssh/config.d/*` + conservative `Host *` defaults)
00524| - `~/.ssh/config.d/00-defaults` - SSH global defaults stub (commented examples only)
00525| - `~/.ssh/config.d/git` - SSH host entries for `github.com` and `gitlab.com` with commented multi-account/Bitwarden examples
00526| - `~/.config/homebrew/` - Brewfiles for GUI apps (macOS casks + mas)
00527| 
00528| SSH files are managed as create-only templates: if `~/.ssh/config` already exists, it is not overwritten. In that case, add `Include ~/.ssh/config.d/*` to your existing config manually to load the managed snippets.
00529| 
00530| ### Tools (via ansible)
00531| 
00532| - **Base**: git, curl, ripgrep, fd, just, build tools
00533| - **Neovim**: >= 0.11.2 with LazyVim dependencies
00534| - **LazyVim deps**: fzf, lazygit, tree-sitter-cli, Node.js
00535| - **Coding Agents** (optional): Claude Code, Codex CLI, CodexBar, OpenCode, Cursor CLI, Copilot CLI, Gemini CLI, SpecStory, Happy, OpenChamber
00536| - **Bitwarden** (optional): Bitwarden CLI (`bw`) via npm, Desktop app (snap/deb on Linux, cask on macOS) on desktop profiles, with zsh completion and SSH agent auto-detection
00537| - **Docker**: OrbStack (macOS) or Docker Engine (Linux)
00538| - **Cargo tools**: pueue (process queue manager)
00539| - **GUI Apps** (macOS): terminals, editors, browsers, utilities via Brewfile
00540| 
00541| ### Bootstrap (installed before ansible)
00542| - **Homebrew** (macOS): Package manager for macOS
00543| - **uv**: Python package manager for ansible
00544| - **mise**: Runtime manager for Node.js and Rust (ensures latest versions)
00545| - **Dev tools**: bat, eza, git-delta, tldr, thefuck, zoxide, direnv, yazi, tmux+tpm, zellij, btop, htop
00546| - **NerdFonts**: Hack N

00918| # CodexBar CLI
00919| 
00920| [CodexBar](https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar) shows usage stats for AI coding tools (Codex, Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini, Copilot, etc.) without logging into each dashboard.
00921| 
00922| - **macOS**: Full menu bar app + CLI
00923| - **Linux**: CLI only
00924| 
00925| ## Installation
00926| 
00927| Installed automatically via the `coding_agents` ansible role. On Linux, the binary is placed at `~/.local/bin/codexbar`.
00928| 
00929| ## Linux Usage
00930| 
00931| On Linux, you **must** pass `--source cli` for the `usage` command. The default source (`auto`/`web`) is macOS-only.
00932| 
00933| ### Check live usage (rate limits / quotas)
00934| 
00935| ```bash
00936| # Claude session/weekly limits
00937| codexbar usage --provider claude --source cli
00938| 
00939| # Other providers
00940| codexbar usage --provider codex --source cli
00941| codexbar usage --provider gemini --source cli
00942| codexbar usage --provider copilot --source cli
00943| 
00944| # JSON output (for scripting / Waybar)
00945| codexbar usage --provider claude --source cli --json --pretty
00946| ```
00947| 
00948| Example output:
00949| 
00950| ```
00951| == Claude 2.1.34 (claude) ==
00952| Session: 14% left [=-----------]
00953| ```
00954| 
00955| ### Check local cost (from JSONL logs, no auth needed)
00956| 
00957| The `cost` command reads local log files (e.g. `~/.claude/`) and doesn't require auth.
00958| 
00959| ```bash
00960| # All providers
00961| codexbar cost
00962| 
00963| # Claude only
00964| codexbar cost --provider claude
00965| 
00966| # JSON output
00967| codexbar cost --provider claude --json --pretty
00968| 
00969| # Force rescan of logs
00970| codexbar cost --refresh
00971| ```
00972| 
00973| Example output:
00974| 
00975| ```
00976| Claude Cost (local)
00977| Today: $0.54 · 851K tokens
00978| Last 30 days: $8.50 · 9.1M tokens
00979| ```
00980| 
00981| ## Shell Aliases
00982| 
00983| Defined in `~/.config/zsh/tools/40_codexbar.zsh`:
00984| 
00985| | Alias | Command | Description |
00986| |-------|---------|-------------|
00987| | `cbu` | `codexbar usage --provider claude --source cli` | Claude usage |
00988| | `cbc` | `codexbar cost --provider claude` | Claude local cost |
00989| | `cbca` | `codexbar cost` | All providers local cost |
00990| 
00991| ## Supported Providers
00992|

00995| ## Tips

01014| # pqsum
01015| 
01016| `pqsum` is a Zsh helper that summarizes `pueue status --json` output into readable queue metrics.
01017| 
01018| - **Function file**: `~/.config/zsh/tools/36_pueue.zsh`
01019| - **Dependencies**: `pueue`, `jq`
01020| - **Optional enhancement**: `column` (for aligned table rendering)
01021| - **Version expectation**: `pueue >= 4.0.0`
01022| 
01023| ## What It Shows
01024| 
01025| `pqsum` prints three sections:
01026| 
01027| 1. `Overall`
01028|    - Total task count
01029|    - Done progress (`done/total`, ASCII progress bar, and `%`)
01030|    - Average duration of finished tasks (`Done` only)
01031|    - Estimated remaining time (ETA)
01032| 2. `Status Breakdown`
01033|    - Aligned table: status, count, progress
01034| 3. `Group Summary`
01035|    - Aligned table with: group, daemon, parallel, total, done, progress, bar, total_spent, avg_done, eta, statuses
01036| 
01037| ## Usage
01038| 
01039| ```bash
01040| # Full summary
01041| pqsum
01042| 
01043| # Single group summary (only that group is displayed)
01044| pqsum -g default
01045| pqsum --group synthesis
01046| 
01047| # Pass any pueue status query/filter through
01048| pqsum status=running
01049| pqsum "status=done order_by end desc first 20"
01050| ```
01051| 
01052| Example output shape:
01053| 
01054| ```text
01055| Pueue Summary
01056| Overall
01057|   Total tasks: 9
01058|   Done progress: 9/9  [============]  100.0%
01059|   Avg done duration: 1m 18s
01060|   Est. remaining (ETA): 0s
01061| 
01062| Status Breakdown
01063|   status  count  progress
01064|   Done    9      100.0%
01065| 
01066| Group Summary
01067|   group      daemon   parallel  total  done  progress  bar           total_spent  avg_done  eta  statuses
01068|   default    Running  1         9      9     100.0%    [============] 4h 12m 8s    1m 18s   0s   Done=9
01069| ```
01070| 
01071| ## Notes
01072| 
01073| - `pqsum` forwards all arguments to `pueue status --json`.
01074| - If `pueue` or `jq` is missing, `pqsum` exits with non-zero and prints an error.
01075| - Average duration only includes tasks whose `Done.start` and `Done.end` are both present.
01076| - `total_spent` is the time span between the earliest and latest timestamps observed in that group (from task `created_at` and status timestamps such as `enqueued_at/start/end`).
01077| - ETA is a coarse estimate based on `remaining * avg_done / max(parallel, 1)`.
01078| - `-g/--group` controls which group rows are shown in the summary output.
01079| - Color is enabled only on TTY output and disabled when `NO_COLOR` is set.
01080| - If `column` is not found, `pqsum` falls back to a plain spacing renderer (still readable).
01081|

01085| - [Pueue Configuration](https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue/wiki/Configuration)
01086| ```

01099| # Ansible Customization Guide
01100| 
01101| This document explains how to customize the ansible setup for your dotfiles.
01102| 
01103| ## Directory Structure
01104| 
01105| After `chezmoi apply`, ansible files are deployed to `~/.ansible/`:
01106| 
01107| ```
01108| ~/.ansible/
01109| ├── ansible.cfg            # Ansible configuration (sets roles_path, inventory)
01110| ├── inventories/
01111| │   └── localhost.ini      # Local inventory
01112| ├── playbooks/
01113| │   ├── base.yml           # Cross-platform essentials
01114| │   ├── linux.yml          # Linux-specific setup
01115| │   └── macos.yml          # macOS-specific setup
01116| └── roles/
01117|     ├── base/              # git, curl, ripgrep, fd, etc.
01118|     ├── homebrew/          # macOS Homebrew installation
01119|     ├── neovim/            # Neovim with version check
01120|     └── lazyvim_deps/      # fzf, lazygit, tree-sitter-cli
01121| ```
01122| 
01123| ## Prerequisites
01124| 
01125| Install ansible and required collections:
01126| 
01127| ```bash
01128| # Install ansible with uv
01129| uv tool install ansible-core
01130| 
01131| # Install community.general collection (for homebrew module)
01132| ansible-galaxy collection install community.general
01133| ```
01134| 
01135| ## Running Playbooks
01136| 
01137| Run from `~/.ansible/` directory (ansible.cfg sets inventory and roles_path automatically):
01138| 
01139| ### Full Setup
01140| 
01141| ```bash
01142| cd ~/.ansible
01143| 
01144| # macOS
01145| ansible-playbook playbooks/macos.yml
01146| 
01147| # Linux
01148| ansible-playbook playbooks/linux.yml
01149| ```
01150| 
01151| ### Specific Tags
01152| 
01153| ```bash
01154| cd ~/.ansible
01155| 
01156| # Only install neovim
01157| ansible-playbook playbooks/macos.yml --tags neovim
01158| 
01159| # Install neovim and its dependencies
01160| ansible-playbook playbooks/macos.yml --tags "neovim,lazyvim_deps"
01161| ```
01162| 
01163| ### Skip Tags
01164| 
01165| ```bash
01166| # Skip tasks requiring sudo (for non-admin users)
01167| ansible-playbook playbooks/linux.yml --skip-tags sudo
01168| ```
01169| 
01170| ### Dry Run
01171| 
01172| ```bash
01173| # Check what would change without applying
01174| ansible-playbook playbooks/macos.yml --check
01175| 
01176| # Verbose output
01177| ansible-playbook playbooks/macos.yml --check -v
01178| ```
01179| 
01180| ## Available Tags
01181| 
01182| | Tag | Description | Requires Sudo |
01183| |-----|-------------|---------------|
01184| | `base` | Essential tools (git, curl, ripgrep, fd, jq) | Linux only |
01185| | `homebrew` | macOS Homebrew installation | No |
01186| | `neovim` | Neovim installation with version check | Linux only |
01187| | `lazyvim_deps` | LazyVim dependencies | Linux only |
01188| | `sudo` | All tasks requiring elevated privileges | Yes |
01189| 
01190| ## Adding New Roles
01191| 
01192| 1. Create role directory structure:
01193| 
01194| ```bash
01195| mkdir -p ~/.ansible/roles/myrole/tasks
01196| mkdir -p ~/.ansible/roles/myrole/defaults  # optional
01197| ```
01198| 
01199| 2. Create tasks file `~/.ansible/roles/myrole/tasks/main.yml`:
01200| 
01201| ```yaml
01202| ---
01203| - name: Install my package (macOS)
01204|   when: ansible_os_family == "Darwin"
01205|   community.general.homebrew:
01206|     name: mypackage
01207|     state: present
01208| 
01209| - name: Install my package (Debian/Ubuntu)
01210|   when: ansible_os_family == "Debian"
01211|   become: true
01212|   tags: [sudo]
01213|   ansible.builtin.apt:
01214|     name: mypackage
01215|     state: present
01216| ```
01217| 
01218| 3. Add role to playbook:
01219| 
01220| ```yaml
01221| # In ~/.ansible/playbooks/macos.yml or linux.yml
01222| roles:
01223|   - role: myrole
01224|     tags: [myrole]
01225| ```
01226| 
01227| ## Syncing Changes Back to Chezmoi
01228| 
01229| After experimenting with changes in `~/.ansible/`, add them back to chezmoi:
01230| 
01231| ```bash
01232| # Copy modified files back to chezmoi source
01233| cp ~/.ansible/roles/myrole/tasks/main.yml ~/.local/share/chezmoi/dot_ansible/roles/myrole/tasks/main.yml
01234| 
01235| # Or use chezmoi re-add
01236| chezmoi re-add ~/.ansible/roles/myrole/tasks/main.yml
01237| ```
01238| 
01239| ## OS Detection
01240| 
01241| Ansible facts used for OS detection:
01242| 
01243| | Fact | macOS | Ubuntu/Debian |
01244| |------|-------|---------------|
01245| | `ansible_os_family` | Darwin | Debian |
01246| | `ansible_distribution` | MacOSX | Ubuntu |
01247| | `ansible_pkg_mgr` | homebrew | apt |
01248| 
01249| Example conditional:
01250| 
01251| ```yaml
01252| - name: macOS only task
01253|   when: ansible_os_family == "Darwin"
01254|   # ...
01255| 
01256| - name: Ubuntu only task
01257|   when: ansible_distribution == "Ubuntu"
01258|   # ...
01259| ```
01260| 
01261| ## Sudo Handling
01262| 
01263| ### Linux
01264| 
01265| Most package installations require sudo. Tasks are tagged with `sudo`:
01266| 
01267| ```yaml
01268| - name: Install package
01269|   become: true
01270|   tags: [sudo]
01271|   ansible.builtin.apt:
01272|     name: mypackage
01273| ```
01274| 
01275| Skip these with `--skip-tags sudo` if you don't have sudo access.
01276| 
01277| ### macOS
01278| 
01279| Homebrew runs as user, no sudo needed. The only exception is system-level changes.
01280| 
01281| ## Troubleshooting
01282| 
01283| ### Syntax Check
01284| 
01285| ```bash
01286| ansible-playbook --syntax-check ~/.ansible/playbooks/base.yml
01287| ```
01288| 
01289| ### Verbose Output
01290| 
01291| ```bash
01292| ansible-playbook ... -vvv
01293| ```
01294| 
01295| ### List Tasks
01296| 
01297| ```bash
01298| ansible-playbook ... --list-tasks
01299| ```
01300| 
01301| ### List Tags
01302| 
01303| ```bash
01304| ansible-playbook ... --list-tags
01305| ```
01306|

01320| ```

01617| ## Maintaining README.md
01618| 
01619| **IMPORTANT**: When adding or modifying configurations, update `README.md` to reflect changes:
01620| 
01621| - **New config files**: Add to "What You Get > Config Files" section
01622| - **New ansible roles/tools**: Add to "What You Get > Tools" section
01623| - **New platforms**: Add to "Supported Platforms" table
01624| - **Changed setup steps**: Update "Quick Setup" section
01625| 
01626| Keep README.md concise and user-focused. Technical details belong in CLAUDE.md or docs/.
01627| 
01628| ## Maintaining Dockerfile
01629| 
01630| **IMPORTANT**: When adding new chezmoi prompts in `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl`, also update `Dockerfile`:
01631| 
01632| 1. Add corresponding `ARG CHEZMOI_*` build argument
01633| 2. Add `--promptBool` or `--promptString` flag to the `chezmoi init` command
01634| 
01635| This ensures Docker testing works with all configuration options.
01636| 
01637| ## Quick Start
01638| 
01639| ```bash
01640| # Install ansible (if not already installed)
01641| uv tool install ansible-core
01642| ansible-galaxy collection install community.general
01643| 
01644| # Apply dotfiles
01645| chezmoi apply
01646| 
01647| # Run ansible manually (from ~/.ansible directory)
01648| cd ~/.ansible && ansible-playbook playbooks/macos.yml
01649| ```
01650| 
01651| ## Architecture
01652| 
01653| ```
01654| chezmoi repo/
01655| ├── dot_* files               → ~/.* (config files)
01656| ├── dot_ansible/              → ~/.ansible/ (ansible playbooks)
01657| ├── run_once_before_*.tmpl    → bootstrap (runs once)
01658| └── run_onchange_after_*.tmpl → ansible (runs on changes)
01659| ```
01660| 
01661| Installation Order:
01662| 
01663| ```
01664| 1. Bootstrap (run_once_before) - installs Homebrew (macOS/Linux), uv, ansible, mise
01665| 2. chezmoi apply - deploys config files + ansible playbooks
01666| 3. Ansible (run_onchange_after) - runs on fresh install + when roles change
01667| 4. Brew bundle (run_onchange_after) - installs GUI apps if enabled
01668| ```
01669| 
01670| ### Auto-run Scripts
01671| 
01672| | Script | Behavior |
01673| |--------|----------|
01674| | `run_once_before_00_bootstrap.sh.tmpl` | Installs Homebrew (macOS and Linux), uv, mise, ansible |
01675| | `run_onchange_after_20_ansible_roles.sh.tmpl` | Runs ansible with all tags |
01676| | `run_onchange_after_30_brew_bundle.sh.tmpl` | Runs brew bundle (if `installBrewApps` enabled) |
01677| 
01678| The onchange script includes SHA256 hashes of all role files. It runs:
01679| 
01680| - **Fresh install**: no previous hash state → triggers run
01681| - **Updates**: any role's `tasks/main.yml` or `defaults/main.yml` changes → triggers run
01682| 
01683| To force re-run all scripts:
01684| 
01685| ```bash
01686| chezmoi state delete-bucket --bucket=scriptState
01687| chezmoi apply
01688| ```
01689| 
01690| ## Chezmoi Commands
01691| 
01692| ```bash
01693| chezmoi diff              # Preview changes
01694| chezmoi apply             # Apply changes
01695| chezmoi apply --dry-run   # Test without applying
01696| chezmoi edit <file>       # Edit source file
01697| chezmoi cd                # Go to source directory
01698| ```
01699| 
01700| ## Ansible Usage
01701| 
01702| Ansible playbooks run automatically via `chezmoi apply` when playbook files change. For manual runs, use `~/.ansible/` directory:
01703| 
01704| ```bash
01705| cd ~/.ansible
01706| 
01707| # Full setup (macOS)
01708| ansible-playbook playbooks/macos.yml
01709| 
01710| # Full setup (Linux)
01711| ansible-playbook playbooks/linux.yml
01712| 
01713| # Specific tags only
01714| ansible-playbook playbooks/macos.yml --tags "neovim,lazyvim_deps"
01715| 
01716| # Skip tags requiring sudo
01717| ansible-playbook playbooks/linux.yml --skip-tags "sudo"
01718| 
01719| # Dry run
01720| ansible-playbook playbooks/macos.yml --check
01721| ```

02226| ## 🤔 What is Spec-Driven Development?
02227| 
02228| Spec-Driven Development **flips the script** on traditional software development. For decades, code has been king — specifications were just scaffolding we built and discarded once the "real work" of coding began. Spec-Driven Development changes this: **specifications become executable**, directly generating working implementations rather than just guiding them.
02229| 
02230| ## ⚡ Get Started
02231| 
02232| ### 1. Install Specify CLI
02233| 
02234| Choose your preferred installation method:
02235| 
02236| #### Option 1: Persistent Installation (Recommended)
02237| 
02238| Install once and use everywhere:
02239| 
02240| ```bash
02241| uv tool install specify-cli --from git+https://github.com/github/spec-kit.git
02242| ```
02243| 
02244| Then use the tool directly:
02245| 
02246| ```bash
02247| # Create new project
02248| specify init <PROJECT_NAME>
02249| 
02250| # Or initialize in existing project
02251| specify init . --ai claude
02252| # or
02253| specify init --here --ai claude
02254| 
02255| # Check installed tools
02256| specify check
02257| ```
02258| 
02259| To upgrade Specify, see the [Upgrade Guide](./docs/upgrade.md) for detailed instructions. Quick upgrade:
02260| 
02261| ```bash
02262| uv tool install specify-cli --force --from git+https://github.com/github/spec-kit.git
02263| ```
02264| 
02265| #### Option 2: One-time Usage
02266| 
02267| Run directly without installing:
02268| 
02269| ```bash
02270| uvx --from git+https://github.com/github/spec-kit.git specify init <PROJECT_NAME>
02271| ```
02272| 
02273| **Benefits of persistent installation:**
02274| 
02275| - Tool stays installed and available in PATH
02276| - No need to create shell aliases
02277| - Better tool management with `uv tool list`, `uv tool upgrade`, `uv tool uninstall`
02278| - Cleaner shell configuration
02279| 
02280| ### 2. Establish project principles
02281| 
02282| Launch your AI assistant in the project directory. The `/speckit.*` commands are available in the assistant.
02283| 
02284| Use the **`/speckit.constitution`** command to create your project's governing principles and development guidelines that will guide all subsequent development.
02285| 
02286| ```bash
02287| /speckit.constitution Create principles focused on code quality, testing standards, user experience consistency, and performance requirements
02288| ```
02289| 
02290| ### 3. Create the spec
02291| 
02292| Use the **`/speckit.specify`** command to describe what you want to build. Focus on the **what** and **why**, not the tech stack.
02293| 
02294| ```bash
02295| /speckit.specify Build an application that can help me organize my photos in separate photo albums. Albums are grouped by date and can be re-organized by dragging and dropping on the main page. Albums are never in other nested albums. Within each album, photos are previewed in a tile-like interface.
02296| ```
02297| 
02298| ### 4. Create a technical implementation plan
02299| 
02300| Use the **`/speckit.plan`** command to provide your tech stack and architecture choices.
02301| 
02302| ```bash
02303| /speckit.plan The application uses Vite with minimal number of libraries. Use vanilla HTML, CSS, and JavaScript as much as possible. Images are not uploaded anywhere and metadata is stored in a local SQLite database.
02304| ```
02305| 
02306| ### 5. Break down into tasks
02307| 
02308| Use **`/speckit.tasks`** to create an actionable task list from your implementation plan.
02309| 
02310| ```bash
02311| /speckit.tasks
02312| ```
02313| 
02314| ### 6. Execute implementation
02315| 
02316| Use **`/speckit.implement`** to execute all tasks and build your feature according to the plan.
02317| 
02318| ```bash
02319| /spe
02320| ... (truncated)
02321| ```

03348| # td - Task management for AI-assisted development
03349| 
03350| **[Documentation](https://marcus.github.io/td/) | [Getting Started](https://marcus.github.io/td/docs/intro) | [GitHub](https://github.com/marcus/td)**
03351| 
03352| A minimalist CLI for tracking tasks across AI coding sessions. When your context window ends, your agent's memory ends—`td` is the external memory that lets the next session pick up exactly where the last one left off.
03353| 
03354| ## Overview
03355| 
03356| `td` is a lightweight CLI for tracking tasks across AI coding sessions. It provides structured handoffs (done/remaining/decisions/uncertain) so new sessions continue from accurate state instead of guessing. Session-based review workflows prevent "works on my context" bugs. Works with Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, and any AI that runs shell commands.
03357| 
03358| **Key Features**: Query-based boards, dependency graphs, epic tracking, powerful query language (TDQ), session analytics, and state machine workflows.
03359| 
03360| ![td](docs/td.png)
03361| 
03362| ## Table of Contents
03363| 
03364| - [Installation](#installation)
03365| - [Quick Start](#quick-start)
03366| - [Claude Code Skill](#claude-code--openai-codex-skill)
03367| - [Core Workflow](#core-workflow)
03368| - [Boards](#boards)
03369| - [Dependencies & Critical Path](#dependencies--critical-path)
03370| - [Query Language (TDQ)](#query-language-tdq)
03371| - [Epics](#epics)
03372| - [Multi-Issue Work Sessions](#multi-issue-work-sessions)
03373| - [File Tracking](#file-tracking)
03374| - [Minor Tasks](#minor-tasks)
03375| - [Analytics & Stats](#analytics--stats)
03376| - [Full Command Reference](#full-command-reference)
03377| - [Live Monitor](#live-monitor)
03378| - [Architecture](#architecture)
03379| - [Development](#development)
03380| - [Release](#release)
03381| - [AI Agent Testimonials](#ai-agent-testimonials)
03382| - [Documentation Site](#documentation-site)
03383| - [Design Philosophy](#design-philosophy)
03384| - [Contributing](#contributing)
03385| - [Support](#support)
03386| - [License](#license)
03387| 
03388| ## The Problem
03389| 
03390| You're using Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, or Copilot. Your AI agent does great work, then the session ends. New session starts. It has no idea what happened. You paste in context. It misunderstands. You correct it. Repeat.
03391| 
03392| Or worse: the agent confidently continues from where it _thinks_ work left off, makes assumptions, and you spend 20 minutes untangling the mess.
03393| 
03394| ## What td Does
03395| 
03396| **Structured handoffs** — Not "here's what I did" but specifically: what's done, what remains, what decisions were made, what's uncertain. The next session doesn't guess.
03397| 
03398| ```bash
03399| td handoff td-a1b2 \
03400|   --done "OAuth flow, token storage" \
03401|   --remaining "Refresh token rotation" \
03402|   --decision "Using JWT for stateless auth" \
03403|   --uncertain "Should tokens expire on password change?"
03404| ```
03405| 
03406| **Session isolation** — Every terminal/context window gets an ID (automatically). The session that writes code can't approve it. A different session has to review. This isn't process theater—it forces actual handoffs and catches the "works on my context" bugs.
03407| 
03408| **Query-based boards** — Organize work with boards that filter issues using TDQ queries. View as swimlanes in the monitor for visual status tracking.
03409| 
03410| **Dependency graphs** — Model dependencies between issues. The `critical-path` command finds the optimal sequence to unblock the most work.
03411| 
03412| **Single command context** — Run `td usage` and your agent gets everything it needs: current focus, pending reviews, open issues, recent decisions. No prompt engineering required.
03413| 
03414| ```
03415| $ td usage
03416| SESSION: marcus-7f3a (started 2h ago)
03417| 
03418| FOCUSED: td-a1b2 "Add OAuth login" [in_progress]
03419|   Last handoff (1h ago):
03420|     Done: OAuth callback, token storage
03421|     Remaining: Refresh rotation, logout flow

03431| ## Installation
03432| 
03433| ### Homebrew (macOS)
03434| 
03435| ```bash
03436| brew install marcus/tap/td
03437| ```
03438| 
03439| ### Download Binary
03440| 
03441| Download pre-built binaries from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/marcus/td/releases). Available for macOS and Linux (amd64/arm64).
03442| 
03443| ### Go Install
03444| 
03445| Requires Go 1.21+:
03446| 
03447| ```bash
03448| go install github.com/marcus/td@latest
03449| ```
03450| 
03451| Ensure `~/go/bin` is in your `$PATH`:
03452| 
03453| ```bash
03454| export PATH="$PATH:$HOME/go/bin"  # Add to ~/.zshrc or ~/.bashrc
03455| ```
03456| 
03457| ### Verify
03458| 
03459| ```bash
03460| td version
03461| ```
03462| 
03463| ## Quick Start
03464| 
03465| ```bash
03466| # Initialize in your project
03467| cd /path/to/your/project
03468| td init

03471| # "Run `td usage --new-session` at conversation start (or after /clear)."

03474| td create "Add user auth" --type feature --priority P1
03475| 
03476| # Start work
03477| td start <issue-id>
03478| ```
03479| 
03480| For complete guides, see the [full documentation](https://marcus.github.io/td/docs/intro).

04873| ### Optional Components
04874| 
04875| During `chezmoi init`, you'll be prompted for optional installs:
04876| 
04877| | Option | Default | Description |
04878| |--------|---------|-------------|

04882| | `installBrewApps` | false | GUI apps via Homebrew Brewfile (casks, mas) |
04883| | `noRoot` | false | Skip sudo-requiring tasks (for servers without root access) |
04884|

04886| 
04887| ## What You Get
04888| 
04889| ### Config Files
04890| 
04891| - `~/.gitconfig` - Git configuration
04892| - `~/.config/nvim/` - Neovim (LazyVim) configuration
04893| - `~/.config/uv/uv.toml` - uv package manager config
04894| - `~/.cargo/config.toml` - Cargo registry mirror config (GFW)
04895| - `~/.npmrc` - npm registry config (official/npmmirror via `useChineseMirror`)
04896| - `~/.config/.bunfig.toml` - Bun global registry config (official/npmmirror via `useChineseMirror`)
04897| - `~/.config/alacritty/` - Alacritty terminal config
04898| - `~/.claude/` - Claude Code settings
04899| - `~/.tmux.conf` - Tmux configuration with TPM plugins
04900| - `~/.local/bin/x` - Cross-platform terminal wrapper for `copy` / `paste` / `open`
04901| - `~/.config/zsh/tools/36_pueue.zsh` - Pueue queue summary helper (`pqsum`)
04902| - `~/.config/zsh/tools/28_tldr.zsh` - `tldrf` helper with `TLDR_LANGUAGES` fallback order
04903| - `~/.config/zsh/tools/95_bitwarden.zsh` - Bitwarden CLI completion + SSH agent socket auto-detection
04904| - `~/.ssh/config` - SSH main config skeleton (create-only: `Include ~/.ssh/config.d/*` + conservative `Host *` defaults)
04905| - `~/.ssh/config.d/00-defaults` - SSH global defaults stub (commented examples only)
04906| - `~/.ssh/config.d/git` - SSH host entries for `github.com` and `gitlab.com` with commented multi-account/Bitwarden examples
04907| - `~/.config/homebrew/` - Brewfiles for GUI apps (macOS casks + mas)
04908| 
04909| SSH files are managed as create-only templates: if `~/.ssh/config` already exists, it is not overwritten. In that case, add `Include ~/.ssh/config.d/*` to your existing config manually to load the managed snippets.
04910| 
04911| ### Tools (via ansible)
04912| 
04913| - **Base**: git, curl, ripgrep, fd, just, build tools
04914| - **Neovim**: >= 0.11.2 with LazyVim dependencies
04915| - **LazyVim deps**: fzf, lazygit, tree-sitter-cli, Node.js
04916| - **Coding Agents** (optional): Claude Code, Codex CLI, CodexBar, OpenCode, Cursor CLI, Copilot CLI, Gemini CLI, SpecStory, Happy, OpenChamber
04917| - **Bitwarden** (optional): Bitwarden CLI (`bw`) via npm, Desktop app (snap/deb on Linux, cask on macOS) on desktop profiles, with zsh completion and SSH agent auto-detection
04918| - **Docker**: OrbStack (macOS) or Docker Engine (Linux)
04919| - **Cargo tools**: pueue (process queue manager)
04920| - **GUI Apps** (macOS): terminals, editors, browsers, utilities via Brewfile
04921| 
04922| ### Bootstrap (installed before ansible)
04923| - **Homebrew** (macOS): Package manager for macOS
04924| - **uv**: Python package manager for ansible
04925| - **mise**: Runtime manager for Node.js and Rust (ensures latest versions)
04926| - **Dev tools**: bat, eza, git-delta, tldr, thefuck, zoxide, direnv, yazi, tmux+tpm, zellij, btop, htop
04927| - **NerdFonts**: Hack Nerd Font for terminal emulators

05427| ## What You Get
05428| 
05429| ### Config Files
05430| 
05431| - `~/.gitconfig` - Git configuration
05432| - `~/.config/nvim/` - Neovim (LazyVim) configuration
05433| - `~/.config/uv/uv.toml` - uv package manager config
05434| - `~/.cargo/config.toml` - Cargo registry mirror config (GFW)
05435| - `~/.npmrc` - npm registry config (official/npmmirror via `useChineseMirror`)
05436| - `~/.config/.bunfig.toml` - Bun global registry config (official/npmmirror via `useChineseMirror`)
05437| - `~/.config/alacritty/` - Alacritty terminal config
05438| - `~/.claude/` - Claude Code settings
05439| - `~/.tmux.conf` - Tmux configuration with TPM plugins
05440| - `~/.local/bin/x` - Cross-platform terminal wrapper for `copy` / `paste` / `open`
05441| - `~/.config/zsh/tools/36_pueue.zsh` - Pueue queue summary helper (`pqsum`)
05442| - `~/.config/zsh/tools/28_tldr.zsh` - `tldrf` helper with `TLDR_LANGUAGES` fallback order
05443| - `~/.config/zsh/tools/95_bitwarden.zsh` - Bitwarden CLI completion + SSH agent socket auto-detection
05444| - `~/.ssh/config` - SSH main config skeleton (create-only: `Include ~/.ssh/config.d/*` + conservative `Host *` defaults)
05445| - `~/.ssh/config.d/00-defaults` - SSH global defaults stub (commented examples only)
05446| - `~/.ssh/config.d/git` - SSH host entries for `github.com` and `gitlab.com` with commented multi-account/Bitwarden examples
05447| - `~/.config/homebrew/` - Brewfiles for GUI apps (macOS casks + mas)
05448| 
05449| SSH files are managed as create-only templates: if `~/.ssh/config` already exists, it is not overwritten. In that case, add `Include ~/.ssh/config.d/*` to your existing config manually to load the managed snippets.
05450| 
05451| ### Tools (via ansible)
05452| 
05453| - **Base**: git, curl, ripgrep, fd, just, build tools
05454| - **Neovim**: >= 0.11.2 with LazyVim dependencies
05455| - **LazyVim deps**: fzf, lazygit, tree-sitter-cli, Node.js
05456| - **Coding Agents** (optional): Claude Code, Codex CLI, CodexBar, OpenCode, Cursor CLI, Copilot CLI, Gemini CLI, SpecStory, Happy, OpenChamber, td, sidecar, specify-cli
05457| - **Bitwarden** (optional): Bitwarden CLI (`bw`) via npm, Desktop app (snap/deb on Linux, cask on macOS) on desktop profiles, with zsh completion and SSH agent auto-detection
05458| - **Docker**: OrbStack (macOS) or Docker Engine (Linux)
05459| - **Cargo tools**: pueue (process queue manager)
05460| - **GUI Apps** (macOS): terminals, editors, browsers, utilities via Brewfile
05461| 
05462| ### Bootstrap (installed before ansible)
05463| - **Homebrew** (macOS): Package manager for macOS
05464| - **uv**: Python package manager for ansible
05465| - **mise**: Runtime manager for Node.js and Rust (ensures latest versions)
05466| - **Dev tools**: bat, eza, git-delta, tldr, thefuck, zoxide, direnv, yazi, tmux+tpm, zellij, btop, htop
05467| - **NerdFonts**: Hack Nerd Font for terminal emulators
05468|
